title: OSHA general industry personal protective equipment practice questions
description: Free OSHA general industry PPE practice questions on 29 CFR 1910 Subpart I. Every answer is explained and linked to the section it comes from.

questions.question: When employees provide their own protective equipment, what does 1910.132(b) make the employer responsible for?

options.A: Assuring its adequacy, including proper maintenance and sanitation
options.B: Nothing, because the employee owns the equipment
options.C: Only reimbursing the purchase price
options.D: Only recording the brand name of the equipment

questions.explanation: Where employees provide their own protective equipment, "the employer shall be responsible to assure its adequacy, including proper maintenance, and sanitation of such equipment."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.132, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When the hazard assessment finds hazards, what does 1910.132(d)(1)(ii) require the employer to do with its PPE selection decisions?

options.A: File them with the OSHA area office
options.B: Keep them confidential from employees
options.C: Communicate them to each affected employee
options.D: Post them only in the employer's head office

questions.explanation: If hazards are present or likely to be present, the employer shall "Communicate selection decisions to each affected employee," as well as select PPE that protects against the hazards and properly fits each affected employee.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.132, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does 1910.132(c) require of the design of all personal protective equipment?

options.A: It must be made in the United States
options.B: It must be bought from a list published by OSHA
options.C: It must be the most expensive model available
options.D: It shall be of safe design and construction for the work to be performed

questions.explanation: The design paragraph says "All personal protective equipment shall be of safe design and construction for the work to be performed."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.132, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An employer replaces the type of face shields its trained employees use, and the earlier training no longer fits the new equipment. What does 1910.132(f)(3) require?

options.A: Nothing, because the employees were already trained once
options.B: Retraining of each such employee
options.C: A new written hazard assessment certification, with no training
options.D: A memo describing the new face shields, with no training

questions.explanation: When the employer has reason to believe a trained employee lacks the required understanding and skill, "the employer shall retrain each such employee." Listed circumstances include where "Changes in the types of PPE to be used render previous training obsolete."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.132, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.132(g), the hazard assessment and training paragraphs of 1910.132 (paragraphs (d) and (f)) apply only to certain sections. Which section is one of them?

options.A: 1910.134, Respiratory protection
options.B: 1910.137, Electrical protective equipment
options.C: 1910.136, Foot protection
options.D: 1910.95, Occupational noise exposure

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.132, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When is an employer not required to pay for replacement PPE?

options.A: When the employee has lost or intentionally damaged the PPE
options.B: When the PPE wore out through normal use
options.C: When the PPE was replaced within the first year
options.D: When the employee works fewer than 40 hours a week

questions.explanation: "The employer must pay for replacement PPE, except when the employee has lost or intentionally damaged the PPE."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.132, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.132(h), which of these is the employer not required to pay for?

options.A: Protective helmets required by 1910.135
options.B: Respirators required by 1910.134
options.C: Replacement PPE after normal wear
options.D: Sunscreen used solely for protection from weather

questions.explanation: The employer is not required to pay for "Ordinary clothing, skin creams, or other items, used solely for protection from weather," which the rule says includes "ordinary sunglasses, and sunscreen."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.132, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When may an employer require an employee to provide or pay for their own PPE?

options.A: Whenever the employee agrees in writing
options.B: Only when the PPE is excepted by paragraphs (h)(2) through (h)(5)
options.C: Whenever the employee is in a probationary period
options.D: Whenever the PPE will also be used at home

questions.explanation: "The employer shall not require an employee to provide or pay for his or her own PPE, unless the PPE is excepted by paragraphs (h)(2) through (h)(5) of this section."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.132, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does 1910.133(a)(4) require for eye and face PPE?

options.A: It is marked with the employee's name
options.B: It is distinctly marked to facilitate identification of the manufacturer
options.C: It is marked with the date of the hazard assessment
options.D: It is marked with the OSHA inspector's initials

questions.explanation: The rule says "Eye and face PPE shall be distinctly marked to facilitate identification of the manufacturer."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.133, Eye and face protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Eye protection must give side protection when there is a hazard from flying objects. What does 1910.133(a)(2) say about detachable side protectors such as clip-on or slide-on side shields?

options.A: They are never acceptable
options.B: They are acceptable only for visitors
options.C: They are acceptable only on prescription glasses
options.D: They are acceptable if they meet the pertinent requirements of the section

questions.explanation: The rule says "Detachable side protectors (e.g. clip-on or slide-on side shields) meeting the pertinent requirements of this section are acceptable."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.133, Eye and face protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A protective helmet was not built to any of the ANSI Z89.1 editions listed in 1910.135(b)(1). When does 1910.135(b)(2) still deem it in compliance?

options.A: When the employer demonstrates it is at least as effective as head protection constructed in accordance with one of those standards
options.B: When it costs less than a listed helmet
options.C: When the employee signs a waiver
options.D: When it has been in use for more than a year

questions.explanation: Under 1910.135(b)(2), "Head protection devices that the employer demonstrates are at least as effective as head protection devices that are constructed in accordance with one of the above consensus standards will be deemed to be in compliance with the requirements of this section."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.135, Head protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Besides falling, rolling or piercing objects, in which situation does 1910.136(a) require protective footwear?

options.A: Whenever the floor is carpeted
options.B: Whenever the employee walks more than one mile per shift
options.C: When the footwear will protect the employee from an electrical hazard, such as a static-discharge or electric-shock hazard, that remains after the employer takes other necessary protective measures
options.D: Whenever the employee works outdoors in the rain

questions.explanation: Protective footwear is also required "when the use of protective footwear will protect the affected employee from an electrical hazard, such as a static-discharge or electric-shock hazard, that remains after the employer takes other necessary protective measures."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.136, Foot protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: On what must employers base their selection of hand protection?

options.A: An evaluation of the hand protection's performance characteristics relative to the tasks, conditions, duration of use and hazards
options.B: The lowest available price
options.C: The glove color the employee prefers
options.D: Whatever brand was used at the employee's last job

questions.explanation: "Employers shall base the selection of the appropriate hand protection on an evaluation of the performance characteristics of the hand protection relative to the task(s) to be performed, conditions present, duration of use, and the hazards and potential hazards identified."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.138, Hand protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: In controlling diseases caused by breathing contaminated air, what does 1910.134 name as the primary objective?

options.A: Giving every employee a dust mask
options.B: Limiting shifts to 4 hours
options.C: Testing employees' lungs every month
options.D: Preventing atmospheric contamination, as far as feasible by accepted engineering control measures

questions.explanation: "The primary objective shall be to prevent atmospheric contamination," accomplished "as far as feasible by accepted engineering control measures." "When effective engineering controls are not feasible, or while they are being instituted, appropriate respirators shall be used."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.134, Respiratory protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An employee's only respirator use is the voluntary use of filtering facepieces (dust masks). What does 1910.134 say about including that employee in the written respiratory protection program?

options.A: The employee must be included and fit tested annually
options.B: The employee must be included after 30 days of use
options.C: Employers are not required to include that employee in the written program
options.D: The employee must be included only if they work night shifts

questions.explanation: "Employers are not required to include in a written respiratory protection program those employees whose only use of respirators involves the voluntary use of filtering facepieces (dust masks)."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.134, Respiratory protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: If an employer determines that voluntary respirator use is permissible, what must the employer give the respirator users?

options.A: A copy of the employer's insurance policy
options.B: The information contained in appendix D to 1910.134
options.C: A NIOSH certification card
options.D: A list of OSHA inspectors in the area

questions.explanation: "If the employer determines that any voluntary respirator use is permissible, the employer shall provide the respirator users with the information contained in appendix D to this section."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.134, Respiratory protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How does 1910.134(e)(4)(i) require the respirator medical questionnaire and examinations to be administered?

options.A: Confidentially, during the employee's normal working hours or at a time and place convenient to the employee
options.B: In a group session with the supervisor present
options.C: Only on the employee's own time, away from the workplace
options.D: By posting the questionnaire on the break-room notice board

questions.explanation: The rule says "The medical questionnaire and examinations shall be administered confidentially during the employee's normal working hours or at a time and place convenient to the employee."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.134, Respiratory protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: After passing a fit test, an employee tells the program administrator that the respirator's fit is unacceptable. What does 1910.134(f)(4) require?

options.A: The employee keeps using the same respirator until the next annual fit test
options.B: The employee is removed from all work that needs a respirator
options.C: The employee pays for a different respirator
options.D: The employee is given a reasonable opportunity to select a different respirator facepiece and to be retested

questions.explanation: In that case "the employee shall be given a reasonable opportunity to select a different respirator facepiece and to be retested."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.134, Respiratory protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An employee who must wear a tight-fitting respirator also wears corrective glasses. What does 1910.134(g)(1)(ii) require?

options.A: The employee takes off the glasses and works without them
options.B: The employee switches to contact lenses
options.C: The employer ensures the glasses are worn in a manner that does not interfere with the seal of the facepiece to the face
options.D: The glasses may break the seal as long as the employee performs a user seal check

questions.explanation: If an employee wears corrective glasses or goggles or other PPE, "the employer shall ensure that such equipment is worn in a manner that does not interfere with the seal of the facepiece to the face of the user."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.134, Respiratory protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An employee wearing an air-purifying respirator detects vapor breakthrough. What does 1910.134(g)(2) require?

options.A: The employee tightens the straps and keeps working
options.B: The employee leaves the respirator use area, and the employer replaces or repairs the respirator before the employee returns to the work area
options.C: The employee finishes the task and reports the problem at the end of the shift
options.D: The employee keeps working but takes shorter breaths

questions.explanation: Employees must leave the respirator use area "If they detect vapor or gas breakthrough, changes in breathing resistance, or leakage of the facepiece," and "the employer must replace or repair the respirator before allowing the employee to return to the work area."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.134, Respiratory protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)
